blogs.title: Airbnb regulations in Nice: what every owner should know in 2026
blogs.author: B&C Conciergerie
blogs.excerpt: Nice has recently adjusted its rules to limit the impact of short-term rentals. The maximum limit for short-term rental has been reduced to 90 days per year for primary residences.

content.introduction: Airbnb regulations in Nice have evolved significantly in 2026. Property owners must now navigate a strict legal framework to avoid penalties and optimize their short-term rental activity.

sections.title: A specific local rule on rental durations
sections.content:
The City of Nice has recently adjusted its rules to further limit the impact of short-term rentals on residential housing.

Primary residence: The maximum limit for short-term rental has been reduced to 90 days per year, down from 120 days previously for primary residences throughout the city. This restriction aims to preserve housing for residents while regulating tourist rentals.

 This rule applies everywhere in Nice since 2025/2026, even though it is particularly emphasized in the most stressed neighborhoods.

Secondary residence in certain high-demand areas: In areas where tourist pressure is strongest (Old Nice, Historic City Center, Riquier-Port-Mont-Boron, West Sector), quotas have been set: only 1.5% of primary residences in each of these sectors can obtain authorization for change of use.

In these same zones, authorization for change of use for a secondary residence is limited to 3 years, non-renewable.

sections.title: What this means for property owners
sections.content:
If the property is your primary residence, you must respect the limit of 90 nights of rental per year, even if you are only absent a few weeks during the year.

If the property is not your primary residence, in high-demand areas, you will need to:
- Obtain authorization for change of use to operate as tourist accommodation
- Comply with municipal quotas
- Plan the 3 years of authorization before any resale or strategy change

sections.title: Some useful regulatory reminders
sections.content:
Declaration at city hall and registration number: mandatory for any Airbnb listing, regardless of property status.

Tourist tax: collected and paid, even though Airbnb facilitates this process.

Penalties: fines can be significant in case of non-compliance - up to several thousand euros if the registration number is missing or if the day limit is exceeded.

sections.title: Why are regulations evolving?
sections.content: Nice faces strong real estate pressure. The municipality seeks to preserve the balance between residential housing, tourist activity, and economic dynamism. This will explains the progressive strengthening of controls and administrative obligations.

sections.title: How to secure your Airbnb activity in Nice?
sections.content:

- Primary or secondary residence
- Condominium status
- Urban planning regulations
- Possible constraints from condominium regulations

A misinterpretation can compromise the project's profitability.

blogs.title: Airbnb or long-term rental in Nice: which option is the most profitable in 2026?
blogs.author: B&C Conciergerie
blogs.excerpt: Nice is one of the most attractive cities in France for real estate investors. For a property owner, the crucial question is often: Airbnb or long-term rental? Which option truly generates the best income?

content.introduction:
Nice is one of the most attractive cities in France for real estate investors. Between international tourism, professional events, and exceptional quality of life, rental demand remains strong year-round.

For a property owner, the crucial question is often: Airbnb or long-term rental? Which option truly generates the best income while remaining compliant with local regulations?

sections.title: Airbnb in Nice: opportunities and constraints
sections.content:
Advantages of short-term rental:
- Higher revenue: A city-center apartment can generate up to 3 to 5 times more than a traditional long-term rental.
- Flexibility: You can block certain periods for your personal use.
- Suited to international tourism: Foreign visitors primarily seek short stays.

Constraints to consider:
- Strict local rules: 90-day limit for primary residences and 3-year authorization for secondary residences in certain neighborhoods.
- Daily management: Responding to travelers, check-in/check-out, cleaning, linen, maintenance.
- Seasonality: High season is very lucrative, but low season requires an effective pricing strategy.

sections.title: Long-term rental: security and stability
sections.content:
Advantages:
- Regular and guaranteed income: Monthly rent ensures a stable cash flow.
- Fewer operational constraints: No frequent check-in/check-out, no cleaning between each stay.
- Administrative simplicity: Fewer declarations and daily monitoring.

Limitations:
- Capped revenue: Monthly rents are often lower than the potential income from a short-term rental.
- Less flexibility: A committed tenant limits personal use of the property.
- Tax impact: Taxation differs depending on the type of rental, with fewer optimization levers.

sections.title: Criteria for choosing the right option
sections.content:
1. Neighborhood and attractiveness: City center, Carré d'Or, or Old Nice are ideal for Airbnb. Less touristy areas are better suited for long-term rental.
2. Owner availability: Airbnb requires regular monitoring.
3. Financial goals: Maximize income or secure stable revenue.
4. Risk tolerance: Airbnb is more profitable but more variable.
5. Regulations: Respecting local quotas and limits is essential.

sections.title: How B&C Conciergerie helps owners decide
sections.content:
At B&C Conciergerie, we support each property owner with a personalized analysis of their property:
- Neighborhood study and rental potential
- Revenue projection: Airbnb vs long-term rental
- Regulatory advice to stay compliant
- Personalized strategy based on your financial goals

Our approach allows you to choose the most profitable option while securing your investment.

faq.answer: Yes, but you need to optimize the listing, adjust pricing, and comply with regulations.

faq.question: Is Airbnb income reliable?
faq.answer: It is higher on average but more variable. Professional management reduces the risk.

faq.answer: Yes. Some owners rent short-term during high season and long-term for the rest of the year.

blogs.title: Airbnb in Nice: new 2026 regulations and what changes for owners
blogs.author: B&C Conciergerie
blogs.excerpt: Since 1 September 2026, the annual rental cap for a primary residence in Nice has been raised back to 120 days per calendar year. Here are the key rules to know in 2026.

content.introduction:
Updated: September 2026

Short-term rental regulations in Nice keep evolving. Since 1 September 2026, an important change affects owners who rent out their primary residence on Airbnb or other short-term rental platforms.

After being lowered to 90 days, the annual rental cap for a primary residence in Nice has now been raised to 120 days per calendar year.

Are you an owner in Nice already renting out your home short-term, or thinking about getting started? Here are the key rules to know in 2026.

sections.title: Primary residence: back to 120 rental days per year
sections.content:
This is one of the main changes in Nice's new regulations.

From 1 September 2026, the maximum number of days a primary residence can be offered as furnished tourist accommodation is set at 120 days per calendar year.

This change therefore replaces the previous 90-day cap.

In practice, if the property is your primary residence, you can now offer it as a tourist rental for up to 120 cumulative days per year, provided you comply with the other applicable obligations.

sections.title: Primary or secondary residence: mind the difference
sections.content:
The distinction is essential.

For a primary residence: this is the home you usually live in as your main residence. In Nice, renting it as furnished tourist accommodation is now possible for up to 120 days per calendar year.

For a secondary residence: the situation is different. Turning a property that is not your primary residence into furnished tourist accommodation may require a change-of-use authorisation.

The rules may also vary depending on the property's location and the regulatory framework that applies to the area.

Before creating an Airbnb listing for a secondary residence in Nice, it is therefore particularly important to check the property's administrative status.

sections.title: Change of use remains a key issue
Declaring and registering the property
sections.content:
Tourist rental regulations are not limited to the number of rental days.

Owners must also check the declaration and registration obligations that apply to their property.

When the property is subject to registration, the number obtained must be displayed on rental listings.

Owners must also meet their obligations regarding the tourist tax and the various declarations related to their activity.

sections.title: What about owners who were limited to 90 days?
sections.content:
This is precisely one of the important consequences of the change that came into force on 1 September 2026.

The cap for primary residences had previously been lowered to 90 days per calendar year.

Nice's regulations now once again set a cap of 120 days.

For the owners concerned, this represents up to 30 additional potential rental days per calendar year.

These extra days can have a significant impact on a property's pricing strategy and income potential, especially during periods of high tourist demand in Nice.

sections.title: Why should you closely follow Airbnb regulations in Nice?
sections.content:
Nice is a particularly dynamic market for short-term rentals.

But local rules change regularly.

For an owner, it is therefore not enough to focus only on the nightly rate or the occupancy rate.

Regulatory compliance must also be an integral part of the rental strategy.

sections.title: How to prepare your property for short-term rental in Nice
B&C Conciergerie supports owners in Nice
sections.content:
At B&C Conciergerie, we support owners in managing their short-term rentals in Nice and on the French Riviera.

Our support covers every operational stage of the rental: preparing the property, creating and optimising the listing, professional photography, dynamic pricing, guest communication, cleaning and linen, guest check-in, maintenance and property follow-up.

We also keep a close eye on changes in local regulations so we can adapt property management whenever necessary.

faq.question: How many days can I rent out my primary residence on Airbnb in Nice in 2026?
faq.answer: Since 1 September 2026, the cap is set at 120 days per calendar year for a primary residence.

faq.question: Does the 90-day limit still exist in Nice?
faq.answer: The previous 90-day cap was replaced by a 120-day cap from 1 September 2026.

faq.question: Can I rent out a secondary residence on Airbnb in Nice?
faq.answer: It may be possible, but the rules differ from those for a primary residence. A change-of-use authorisation may be required. It is recommended to check the property's exact situation with the relevant authorities before renting it out.

faq.question: Can the regulations change again?
faq.answer: Yes. Rules on furnished tourist accommodation can change at both national and local level. It is therefore important to check official information regularly.

blogs.title: Primary or secondary residence: what are the Airbnb rules in Nice in 2026?
blogs.author: B&C Conciergerie
blogs.excerpt: Before renting out an apartment on Airbnb in Nice, one question is essential: is the property your primary or your secondary residence? Maximum duration, change of use, registration, co-ownership: the key points to know.

content.introduction:
Updated: September 2026

Would you like to rent out an apartment on Airbnb in Nice? Even before creating your listing, one question is essential: is the property your primary residence or your secondary residence?

This distinction matters because the rules that apply to short-term rentals are not the same.

Maximum rental duration, change of use, registration, co-ownership… B&C Conciergerie explains the key points to know before renting out your property short-term in Nice.

sections.title: What is a primary residence?
sections.content:
A primary residence is the home usually occupied by its owner or tenant.

In the context of tourist rentals, this status is particularly important because, under certain conditions, it allows you to rent out your home occasionally without following exactly the same regime as a secondary residence.

In Nice, since 1 September 2026, a primary residence can be rented as furnished tourist accommodation for up to 120 days per calendar year.

sections.title: How many days can you rent out your primary residence on Airbnb in Nice?
sections.content:
The cap in Nice is now 120 days per calendar year.

This means an owner who lives in their home as a primary residence can list it on Airbnb or another short-term rental platform when they are not using it, within the regulatory cap.

This rule may apply, for example, to an owner who wants to rent out their apartment during their holidays, on certain weekends or when they are away for several weeks.

Be careful, though: staying within the 120-day limit does not exempt you from checking the other administrative obligations that apply to the property.

sections.title: What is a secondary residence?
sections.content:
A secondary residence is a property that is not its occupant's primary residence.

It may be, for example, an apartment bought as an investment, a pied-à-terre in Nice or a home occupied only a few weeks a year.

For this type of property, tourist rental rules can be more restrictive.

Unlike a primary residence rented out occasionally, renting a secondary residence to tourists may in particular require a change-of-use authorisation.

sections.title: Can you rent out a secondary residence on Airbnb in Nice?
What is a change of use?
sections.content:
A change of use is an administrative procedure that concerns, in particular, turning a property intended as a home into premises used for short-term tourist rental.

In some situations, an owner wishing to operate a secondary residence as furnished tourist accommodation must obtain this authorisation from the relevant local authority.

Change of use (changement d'usage) should not be confused with change of designated purpose (changement de destination): these are two different legal concepts.

The situation must therefore be assessed for each property.

sections.title: Can the property's location in Nice change the rules?
sections.content:
Yes.

Nice's regulations on furnished tourist accommodation include specific measures for certain geographical areas.

The exact location of the property can therefore affect the possibilities of obtaining a change of use and the procedures required.

Before investing in a property with the aim of offering it mainly as a short-term rental, it is therefore best to check the regulations that apply precisely to that area.

sections.title: What if you buy an apartment specifically for Airbnb?
Can co-ownership rules prohibit Airbnb?
sections.content:
This is another important point to check.

When a property is located in a co-ownership building, its rules may contain provisions on how the apartments can be used.

Before starting a short-term rental activity, it is therefore recommended to read the co-ownership rules carefully and, if in doubt, seek advice from a qualified professional.

sections.title: Do you need to declare your property even if it is your primary residence?
sections.content:
The fact that a property is a primary residence does not mean that no formalities are required.

Owners must check the declaration and registration formalities that apply in Nice.

When a registration number is required, it must be displayed on listings published on rental platforms.

The obligations related to the tourist tax and associated declarations must also be met.

sections.title: Primary or secondary residence: which option suits you best?
sections.content:
There is no single strategy that works for every owner.

Someone who simply wants to earn income from their apartment while on holiday will not have the same needs as an investor with a property intended mainly for short-term rental.

Before getting started, it is therefore useful to determine:
the property's status → the applicable rules → the number of rental days possible → the costs → the income potential.

This analysis gives a much more realistic view of the project.

blogs.title: Airbnb change of use in Nice: procedures, affected neighbourhoods and rules in 2026
blogs.author: B&C Conciergerie
blogs.excerpt: Before publishing your Airbnb listing in Nice, one concept keeps coming up: change of use. Procedures, areas subject to quotas, how it differs from the registration number: the key points to know in 2026.

content.introduction:
Updated: September 2026

Do you own an apartment in Nice and want to offer it as a short-term rental on Airbnb, Booking.com or another platform?

Before publishing your listing, one concept keeps coming up: change of use.

This authorisation may be required when a property intended as a home is operated as furnished tourist accommodation. In Nice, where short-term rentals are particularly widespread, regulations govern this activity and some rules may vary depending on the property's situation and location.

Here are the key points to know in 2026.

sections.title: What is a change of use?
sections.content:
A change of use is an administrative procedure related to how a property is used.

When a property intended as a home is turned into furnished tourist accommodation repeatedly offered to short-stay guests who do not live there, a change-of-use authorisation may be required.

This procedure aims in particular to preserve the balance between housing for residents and tourist accommodation.

In Nice, this question should therefore be examined before starting a regular short-term rental activity.

sections.title: Who is affected by change of use in Nice?
sections.content:
It mainly depends on how the property is used.

You rent out your primary residence: if the property really is your primary residence and you rent it out occasionally while you are away, the regime is different from the one applying to a property dedicated to tourist rental. Since 1 September 2026, a primary residence can be rented as furnished tourist accommodation in Nice for up to 120 days per calendar year, provided the other applicable obligations are met.

You want to rent out a secondary residence: the situation is different when the property is not your primary residence. Renting a secondary residence to tourists may require prior change-of-use authorisation.

It is therefore important to check the property's administrative status before creating the listing and, above all, before accepting the first bookings.

sections.title: Why does the property's address matter?
sections.content:
Not all short-term rental projects should be assessed in the same way.

In Nice, local regulations take the location of properties into account, and certain areas are subject to specific rules.

Very touristy areas, or those with a high concentration of furnished tourist accommodation, may in particular be subject to authorisation quotas.

The possibility of obtaining an authorisation therefore does not depend solely on the property: its address and the area it is in may also have an impact.

sections.title: Which areas of Nice are subject to quotas?
How do you apply for a change of use in Nice?
Change of use and registration number: are they the same thing?
sections.content:
No.

This is a common confusion.

The registration number identifies furnished tourist accommodation administratively and may need to appear on listings published on platforms.

Change of use, on the other hand, concerns the authorisation to use a property intended as a home as furnished tourist accommodation in situations where this authorisation is required.

Obtaining a registration number therefore does not necessarily mean that all the other required authorisations have been obtained.

sections.title: Change of use and change of designated purpose: what is the difference?
sections.content:
These two concepts are also different.

Change of use (changement d'usage) falls under the regulations governing the use of residential premises.

Change of designated purpose (changement de destination) falls under planning law and concerns the legal designation of premises.

Depending on the project, the procedures required may therefore differ.

If in doubt about a property's situation, it is best to consult the relevant authorities or a specialist professional.

sections.title: Watch out for co-ownership rules
sections.content:
The administrative authorisation is not the only thing to check.

If your apartment is in a co-ownership building, you also need to consult its co-ownership rules.

Some clauses may govern how the apartments are used or which activities are permitted in the building.

An owner wishing to start a short-term rental activity must therefore examine:
municipal regulations + the property's administrative status + the co-ownership rules.

blogs.title: Listing your apartment on Airbnb in Nice: the complete checklist before your first booking
blogs.author: B&C Conciergerie
blogs.excerpt: Regulations, preparing the property, photos, pricing, cleaning, guest management: here is the complete checklist for Airbnb owners in Nice to get off to a good start before the first booking.

content.introduction:
Updated: September 2026

Do you own an apartment in Nice and want to list it on Airbnb?

Between regulations, preparing the property, photos, pricing, cleaning and guest management, a successful short-term rental doesn't happen by chance.

Before welcoming your first guest, here is the complete checklist for Airbnb owners in Nice to prepare their property and get off to a good start.

sections.title: 1. Check that your property can be rented short-term
2. Prepare a guest-friendly property
3. Take care of the decor without overloading the apartment
sections.content:
On Airbnb, the first impression starts even before the guest arrives.

It starts with the photos.

It is therefore important to create a pleasant, coherent interior.

Opt for bright, fairly neutral and warm decor, while keeping a few elements that give the property character.

In Nice, Mediterranean-inspired decor can work particularly well: natural materials, light colours, touches of blue, beige, wood or greenery.

The goal is not to turn the apartment into an impersonal hotel, but to create a home that guests can easily picture themselves in.

sections.title: 4. Take great photos
5. Create an Airbnb listing that makes people want to book
sections.content:
A good listing isn't simply about writing "lovely apartment near the sea".

The title and description must immediately highlight the property's real strengths.

For example:
"Balcony • Air conditioning • 2 min from the Promenade • Ideal for couples"

is generally far more informative than a simple:
"Lovely apartment in Nice"

The description should then answer the guest's main questions:

Roughly where is the property? How many people can stay? What amenities are available? Is there air conditioning? A balcony? A lift? Parking? How far are the beach and public transport?

A clear listing also limits unpleasant surprises and therefore negative reviews.

sections.title: 6. Set the right nightly rate
7. Set your cleaning fees correctly
8. Organise check-ins and check-outs
9. Plan for the unexpected before it happens
10. Prepare your guest communication
11. Prepare the property to earn its first reviews
sections.content:
The first bookings are particularly important.

A new property without reviews needs to build its reputation quickly.

The goal is therefore not just to get bookings, but to offer an experience good enough to earn great first reviews.

Cleanliness, communication, photos that match reality, comfort and an easy arrival are essential.

A few excellent reviews can then make subsequent bookings easier.

sections.title: 12. Track performance after going live

blogs.title: Private concierge in Nice: personalised management of your property, wherever you are
blogs.author: B&C Conciergerie
blogs.excerpt: Entrusting your apartment to a concierge service means, above all, entrusting your property to someone you can trust. As an independent private concierge in Nice, I personally support owners, whether they live in Nice, elsewhere in France or abroad.

content.introduction:
Entrusting your apartment to a concierge service is not simply about delegating guest messages, cleaning or check-ins.

It is, above all, about entrusting your property to someone you can trust.

That is precisely the vision I wanted to give B&C Conciergerie: to offer owners in Nice and the surrounding area a more human, closer and, above all, more personalised management service.

I am an independent private concierge in Nice, and I personally support owners who want to rent out their apartment or house short-term, whether they live in Nice, elsewhere in France or on the other side of the world.

sections.title: A trusted person on site when you are far away
sections.content:
Owning an apartment in Nice when you live hundreds or thousands of kilometres away can quickly become complicated.

Who checks the property?
Who welcomes the guests?
Who steps in when an appliance breaks down?
Who coordinates a tradesperson?
Who makes sure the cleaning has been done properly?

And above all: who really looks after your apartment when you're not there?

My role is precisely to be that person on site.

I want every owner to know they have a contact in Nice who knows their property and can step in whenever a situation requires it.

Whether you live in Paris, London, New York, Montreal or elsewhere, distance shouldn't stop you from renting out your property with peace of mind.

sections.title: I don't want to manage hundreds of apartments
sections.content:
B&C Conciergerie is built on a deliberate choice: prioritising the quality of the portfolio over its size.

My goal is not to accumulate hundreds of properties under management.

I prefer to manage a smaller portfolio so I can devote enough time and attention to each one.

Why? Because every property is different.

A studio near the Port of Nice isn't managed exactly like a family apartment in Fabron, a sea-view residence or a villa on the French Riviera.

Every owner also has their own expectations.

Some want to follow their bookings regularly. Others live abroad and prefer to delegate practically all of the management. Some stay in their apartment for several weeks a year, while others use it purely as a rental investment.

Management must therefore adapt to the owner and the property, not the other way round.

sections.title: I want to truly know every property I manage
sections.content:
For me, managing an apartment properly means knowing it.

Knowing its appliances.
Knowing where the electricity meter is.
Knowing how the water heater or air conditioning works.
Knowing its little quirks.
Knowing the building and its access points.
Quickly identifying the right professional to call when work is needed.

These are sometimes details, but when you are thousands of kilometres away and a problem arises during a guest's stay, these details become essential.

That is also why I want to keep a human-scale operation.

sections.title: Step-by-step support
sections.content:
Some owners contact me with a property already listed on Airbnb.

Others have just bought their apartment and don't yet know where to start.

My role is to support them step by step.

We can start by studying the property and its potential, then prepare it before it is first rented out.

Then come the various stages: preparation and furnishing, photography, creating or optimising the listing, pricing strategy, organising cleaning and linen, preparing check-ins and setting up guest communication.

Once the property is being rented, the support continues.

I remain available to follow bookings, reply to guests, coordinate any necessary work and keep the owner informed of what is happening in their apartment.

sections.title: Your apartment doesn't become just "one more property"
sections.content:
This is probably the point I care about most.

When you entrust me with your apartment, I don't want it to become just a number in a portfolio of hundreds of properties.

I want to know its story, its strengths, its weaknesses and the improvements that can be made.

I also want to know your expectations as an owner.

This knowledge makes for much more precise management and better decisions when an unexpected situation arises.

sections.title: A direct relationship with your concierge
sections.content:
By choosing independent, human-scale management, you also know who is looking after your property.

You don't need to re-explain your situation to different contacts every time you have a question.

The relationship with the owner is direct.

For me, this closeness is particularly important with owners who live abroad.

When thousands of kilometres separate you from your apartment, having an identifiable person on site brings real peace of mind.

sections.title: Management tailored to each owner
sections.content:
I don't want to impose exactly the same way of working on everyone.

Some owners want to be kept informed regularly and follow their bookings closely.

Others simply want to receive their updates and know that everything is being handled properly.

Some use their property themselves several times a year and want to block certain periods.

Every situation is different.

Together, we therefore define the level of support and communication that suits you.

sections.title: From the first listing to day-to-day follow-up
Do you live abroad and own an apartment in Nice?
sections.content:
Distance is not a problem.

I work with owners living in Nice as well as those based elsewhere in France or abroad.

Your apartment can be in Nice or the surrounding area: what matters is being able to build a relationship of trust and an organisation suited to your situation.

You naturally keep visibility over your property and your bookings, while I handle the management on site.

sections.title: Behind B&C Conciergerie, there is a person
sections.content:
I want to grow B&C Conciergerie while keeping what, in my eyes, is its true value: closeness.

Growing, yes.

But not at the expense of management quality.

I would rather support fewer owners, truly know their properties and build a lasting relationship with them than multiply properties to the point of losing that closeness.

Your property deserves management that suits it.

And when you are far away, you deserve to know that someone on site is really looking after your property.
